title: Paramartha Guru Tale 94
summary: A visiting assembly of ten visiting scholars from Kanchipuram arrived at the ashram at noon.
full_text:
A visiting assembly of ten visiting scholars from Kanchipuram arrived at the ashram at noon.

Guru Paramartha wished to display supreme Ayurvedic hospitality.

Madayan suggested: 'Bitter gourd is the king of purifying vegetables! We shall prepare a nine-course banquet consisting entirely of bitter gourd: bitter gourd soup, fried bitter gourd, boiled bitter gourd with neem, bitter gourd chutney, and bitter gourd pudding!'

The feast was served on clean banana leaves.

The ten visiting scholars took their seats, smiled, and dipped their fingers into the first course: bitter gourd soup.

The overwhelming, eye-watering, throat-searing bitterness struck their palates!

One scholar gagged; another turned pale; a third spit his mouthful into his palm!

They tried the fried gourd: more bitterness! They tried the chutney: pure gall!

The chief visiting scholar rose from his mat, his face pale: 'Guru Paramartha! Did we come to a hermitage or a poison refinery? We asked for lunch, not a therapeutic execution!'

The ten scholars marched out of the ashram, leaving their half-eaten banana leaves behind.

Guru Paramartha sat down and tasted the soup: 'PHTHOO! Madayan, this is vile!'

Madayan sighed: 'Scholars of Kanchipuram lack spiritual endurance; let us give the soup to the village goats!'

Even the goats sniffed the bitter gourd and walked away in disgust.
moral: Serving pure bitterness under the guise of medicinal hospitality clears the room of guests.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Paramartha Guru Tale 94"?
options: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By running away from every problem
